headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires data centers and other large energy users (25 MW or more) to bear the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, environmental groups (e.g., Virginia Conservation Network, Sierra Club), Dominion Energy.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Shifts Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed HB 1393, requiring facilities using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity, thereby preventing these costs from being passed to other customers. This legislation aims to address concerns about rising utility bills for residents due to data center energy demands.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandated
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities providing water to data centers report monthly water consumption data to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency on the industry's water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Virginia Conservation Network, Sierra Club, Virginia League of Conservation Voters), local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Potentially data center industry (due to increased reporting burden and scrutiny).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, with the numbers to be aggregated and made available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the significant water consumption by data centers and provide credible data for public access.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
short_summary: This bill requires new high energy use facilities (HEUF), primarily data centers, to conduct site assessments examining sound profiles on nearby residential units and schools, and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community advocates, environmental groups (e.g., Virginia Conservation Network), Delegate Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate interests.
news_headline: Virginia Adds New Restrictions on Data Center Siting
news_summary: Virginia passed HB 153, establishing a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) of 100 MW or more, requiring sound assessments near homes and schools within 500 feet. Localities can also now require assessments of impacts on water resources, agriculture, and historic sites before approving projects.
